options: The Variable Fee Approach (VFA), which applies automatically to all unit-linked policies.
The Premium Allocation Approach (PAA), which applies by default to all short-term and long-term contracts.
The Historical Cost Model, which carries contracts at original unearned premium.
The General Measurement Model (GMM), also known as the Building Block Approach (BBA), comprising present value of future cash flows, risk adjustment, and CSM.
explanationCorrect: GMM (or Building Block Approach) is the core default measurement model under Ind AS 117. PAA is an optional simplification for short-term contracts, and VFA is a mandatory modification strictly for direct participating contracts.
explanationIncorrect: GMM forms the foundational baseline against which all other measurement models are evaluated.

source: FT-IGN 31, Variable Fee Approach (VFA) Eligibility Criteria
question: Under Ind AS 117 and FT-IGN 31, which mandatory criteria must a contract satisfy to be eligible for the Variable Fee Approach (VFA)?
options: The contract must have a coverage duration of less than twelve months.

The contract must be a direct participating contract where contract terms specify that the policyholder participates in a share of a clearly identified pool of underlying items, expects to receive a substantial share of fair value returns, and cash flows vary directly with those returns.
The contract must have zero investment guarantees and zero cash surrender value.
The contract must be an annual renewable group health policy written on an employer-employee basis.
explanationCorrect: VFA applies strictly to direct participating contracts meeting three conditions: defined pool of underlying items, substantial share of fair value returns to policyholders, and high proportion of cash flow variability linked to those returns.
explanationIncorrect: VFA reflects the economic substance of asset-management-like insurance contracts (such as unit-linked or participating with-profits).

source: FT-IGN 31, Ind AS 117 Contract Boundaries (Para 34)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 34, when do cash flows fall outside the contract boundary of an existing insurance contract?
options: When the insurer has the practical ability to reassess the risks of the particular policyholder and, as a result, can set a price or level of benefits that fully reflects those risks, OR has the practical ability to reprice the portfolio.
When the policyholder reaches the age of sixty-five years.
When the policyholder stops paying premiums for more than thirty days.
When the insurance contract has been in force for more than ten calendar years.
explanationCorrect: Para 34 defines the contract boundary: cash flows are outside the boundary if the entity can fully reprice the individual risk or the portfolio to reflect current risk expectations.
explanationIncorrect: Contract boundaries dictate what future cash flows (e.g. renewal premiums) must be included in present value calculations.

source: FT-IGN 31, Accounting for Reinsurance Contracts Held
question: Under Ind AS 117 and FT-IGN 31, how must an insurer value and present reinsurance contracts held (ceded reinsurance)?
options: Reinsurance assets must always equal 100% of the gross reserves ceded.

Reinsurance contracts held must be valued separately from underlying insurance contracts, cannot be netted off against gross liabilities, and must incorporate an explicit adjustment for non-performance risk (counterparty credit risk) of the reinsurer.
Reinsurance contracts held are exempt from discounting and risk adjustment requirements.
Reinsurance cash flows must be netted directly against gross insurance liabilities on the balance sheet.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 strictly prohibits netting reinsurance against gross insurance liabilities. Reinsurance held is evaluated as a separate asset, with mandatory adjustment for reinsurer default/non-performance risk.
explanationIncorrect: Gross reporting of liabilities and separate reinsurance asset measurement is a fundamental transparency principle.

source: FT-IGN 31, Discounting: Bottom-Up vs Top-Down Method
question: Under Ind AS 117 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.14, what is the core structural difference between the 'Bottom-Up' and 'Top-Down' approaches for determining liability discount curves?
options: Bottom-Up is used in general insurance, while Top-Down is used exclusively in life insurance.
Bottom-Up applies to policy liabilities, while Top-Down applies exclusively to shareholder equity.
Bottom-Up discounts only cash flows up to five years, while Top-Down discounts cash flows beyond five years.
Bottom-Up starts with a liquid risk-free yield curve and adds an illiquidity premium; Top-Down starts with reference asset portfolio yields and removes credit risk and market risk premiums.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117, Bottom-Up adjusts risk-free rates upward for liability illiquidity; Top-Down adjusts reference asset yields downward for expected and unexpected credit losses, arriving at conceptually equivalent discount rates.
explanationIncorrect: Both approaches aim to capture the liquidity characteristics of the insurance liability cash flows.

source: FT-IGN 31, Contractual Service Margin (CSM) Release & Coverage Units
question: Under Ind AS 117, how is the Contractual Service Margin (CSM) systematically recognized in insurance revenue over the coverage period?
options: Released proportionally based on the fair market value of company equity.
Straight-line amortized over the contractual premium payment term.
Recognized fully in the first year of policy issuance to maximize initial shareholder dividend capacity.
Based on 'coverage units' reflecting the quantity of benefits provided under a contract and its expected coverage duration, recognizing revenue as insurance service is delivered.
explanationCorrect: CSM is released into insurance revenue over time based on coverage units, which reflect the volume of service provided in each period and expected duration.
explanationIncorrect: Coverage units ensure unearned profit (CSM) emerges in profit or loss in lockstep with the provision of insurance coverage.

source: FT-IGN 31, Experience Adjustments vs Changes in Future Assumptions
question: Under the General Measurement Model (GMM) of Ind AS 117, how are current-period cash flow experience variances treated compared to changes in estimates of future cash flows?
options: Both current experience variances and future assumption changes adjust the CSM.
Both current experience variances and future assumption changes are recognized immediately in P&L.
Experience variances adjust the CSM, while future assumption changes are recognized in OCI.
Current-period experience variances (e.g., higher claims paid today) are recognized immediately in profit or loss; changes in assumptions relating to future service adjust the remaining CSM.
explanationCorrect: Current-period experience variances relate to past/current service and flow immediately through profit or loss. Changes in estimates relating to future coverage periods adjust the unearned profit margin (CSM).
explanationIncorrect: Understanding what unlocks CSM versus what hits P&L immediately is a critical technical accounting distinction.

source: FT-IGN 31, Transition Approaches under Ind AS 117
question: When an insurer transitions to Ind AS 117 on the transition date, which hierarchy of transition methods is prescribed by the standard and evaluated by the Auditing Actuary?
options: The Modified Retrospective Approach is prohibited under Indian accounting standards.
The Fair Value Approach is mandatory for all Indian insurers under IRDAI transition circulars.
The insurer may freely select any transition method based on shareholder preference.
Full Retrospective Approach (FRA) is mandatory unless impracticable; if impracticable, the insurer must choose between the Modified Retrospective Approach (MRA) and the Fair Value Approach (FVA).
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 mandates Full Retrospective Approach unless impracticable. Demonstrating impracticability requires rigorous objective evidence before falling back to MRA or Fair Value Approach.
explanationIncorrect: The Auditing Actuary must critically audit management's justification if FRA is claimed to be impracticable.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.8 (Auditing Actuary & Appointed Actuary Protocol)
question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.8, what is the professional protocol governing interactions between the Auditing Actuary and the audited insurer's Appointed Actuary?
options: The Appointed Actuary has a statutory right to refuse to speak with the Auditing Actuary.
The Auditing Actuary must report all minor computational queries directly to the Board of Directors without contacting the AA.
The Auditing Actuary must communicate with the Appointed Actuary exclusively through formal registered legal notices.
Both actuaries must maintain open, professional communication, establish an agreed audit timetable, share data and models collegially, and document technical discussions formally.
explanationCorrect: Section 3.8 requires structured, professional collaboration: clear communication, advance scheduling, respectful technical challenge, and formal documentation of queries and responses.
explanationIncorrect: Effective audits depend on professional collegiality and timely information exchange between actuarial peers.

source: FT-IGN 31 & SA 620, Evaluating Competence and Objectivity of Experts
question: Under ICAI SA 620, what must the statutory financial auditor and lead audit partner evaluate prior to placing reliance on the Auditing Actuary?
options: Verify that the Auditing Actuary holds an equity stake in the audited insurer.
Evaluate the Auditing Actuary's professional competence, technical capabilities, resources, and objectivity (including independence from the audited insurer).
Ensure the Auditing Actuary has served as an employee of the audited insurer within the past 12 months.
Confirm that the Auditing Actuary is the lowest bidder in the commercial audit procurement tender.
explanationCorrect: SA 620 requires the auditor to formally assess the expert's professional competence, capabilities, and objectivity (confirming absence of conflicts of interest and independence threats).
explanationIncorrect: Auditor reliance on an expert is legally defective if expert competence and independence are not evaluated and documented.

source: FT-IGN 31, Data Reconciliation between GL and Actuarial Models
question: During the audit of insurance liabilities, what mandatory data verification procedure must the Auditing Actuary conduct under FT-IGN 31?
options: Assume all data ingested into actuarial models is complete if signed by the IT database administrator.
Perform end-to-end reconciliation between policy administration systems, general ledger accounting feeds, and the input datasets ingested into actuarial valuation models.
Data reconciliation is the exclusive duty of external statutory auditors; actuaries ignore source data feeds.
Verify only a single policy record and extrapolate data accuracy across the entire portfolio.
explanationCorrect: Reconciling policy administration source data, financial ledgers, and actuarial model inputs is a fundamental audit control to ensure completeness and accuracy of cash flow projections.
explanationIncorrect: Garbage in, garbage out: actuarial models are only as reliable as the underlying reconciled accounting data.

source: FT-IGN 31, Materiality Benchmarks in Actuarial Audits
question: When establishing materiality for testing actuarial liability misstatements under FT-IGN 31, which balance sheet and P&L metrics are primarily evaluated?
options: Performance materiality evaluated against Contractual Service Margin (CSM), Liability for Incurred Claims (LIC), Liability for Remaining Coverage (LRC), and Net Asset Value (Equity).
A single fixed threshold of Rs. 10 Lakhs is applied to all insurers regardless of scale.
Materiality is defined strictly by the maximum penalty fine that IRDAI can levy.
Materiality is evaluated solely against the insurer's annual advertising budget.
explanationCorrect: Materiality in insurance audits is calibrated against key insurance line items: CSM, LRC, LIC, total liabilities, and net equity, ensuring misstatements that impact solvency or revenue emergence are flagged.
explanationIncorrect: Materiality benchmarks must be tailored to insurance-specific financial statement aggregates.

source: FT-IGN 31, Strict Dual-Role Independence Prohibition
question: Can an actuarial consulting firm provide both statutory reserving valuation services (Appointed Actuary support) and the external Auditing Actuary assurance to the same insurer in the same financial year?
options: Permitted provided the consulting assignment is completed before the audit commences.
Permitted if the insurer's audit committee pays separate billing invoices for the two services.
Permitted provided the firm uses two different actuarial analysts under the same engagement partner.
Strictly prohibited; providing both valuation preparation and audit assurance creates an irreconcilable self-review threat that destroys auditor independence under ICAI and IAI codes.
explanationCorrect: A firm cannot audit its own work. Preparing valuation figures while simultaneously acting as the auditing actuary violates fundamental independence rules and constitutes grave misconduct.
explanationIncorrect: The self-review threat cannot be mitigated by internal Chinese walls within the same actuarial firm.

source: FT-IGN 31, Reporting to Those Charged With Governance (TCWG) under SA 260
question: Under ICAI SA 260 and FT-IGN 31, what specific actuarial matters should be communicated by the audit team to the Board Audit Committee (TCWG)?
options: The daily attendance records of junior actuarial analysts working on the audit.
Private salary and bonus structures of the actuarial department employees.
The commercial software licensing fees paid by the insurer to its modeling vendors.
Significant qualitative aspects of actuarial practices, key assumption sensitivities, contentious model changes, post-model adjustments, and any material unadjusted valuation differences.
explanationCorrect: SA 260 communications with Audit Committees must cover qualitative accounting choices, key assumption judgments, model governance issues, management overlays (PMAs), and unresolved differences.
explanationIncorrect: Transparent communication with TCWG ensures the board is fully informed on subjective actuarial risks.

source: FT-IGN 31, Audit Report Modifications & Uncorrected Misstatements
question: Where an insurer's management refuses to correct an actuarial reserving understatement that exceeds performance materiality, what must the Auditing Actuary recommend to the statutory auditor?
options: Agree to an off-the-record compromise splitting the valuation difference by fifty percent.
Instruct the insurer to omit the insurance liability note entirely from the published annual report.
Issue an unqualified clean audit opinion while filing an anonymous complaint with the local police.
Recommend issuing a modified audit opinion (Qualified Opinion or Adverse Opinion) under ICAI SA 705, detailing the nature and quantified financial impact of the misstatement.
explanationCorrect: If material actuarial misstatements remain unadjusted, the auditing actuary must recommend a qualified or adverse audit opinion under SA 705, detailing the technical divergence and financial impact.
explanationIncorrect: Auditors cannot issue clean opinions on materially misstated actuarial balance sheets.
